run.name: 19-logo-house-door
run.finalText:
The wordmark's opacity is stuck at 0 because the entrance used the layer's rest value, which was 0. I'm setting explicit keyframes to fix it.
I built the Hearth sting as a 4 s composition. It ends on the full lockup, with the mark on the left and "Hearth" to its right. I checked it only in contact-sheet frames, not played back in real time, and I didn't run the critic.

- **Look:** dark warm brown background (#2a1a14), cream house outline and wordmark, and one amber accent.
- **0–1.2 s:** the **house** outline (a pentagon) draws itself on, centred on screen.
- **1.1–1.9 s:** the amber **door** appears inside the house, then swings open on its left edge. A pale amber **glow** shows behind it.
- **1.9–2.8 s:** the mark slides left to its final position.
- **2.3–3.1 s:** the **word** "Hearth" fades in and slides out to the right of the mark, with an ease-out.
- **3.1–4 s:** the lockup holds.

The open door is a narrow sliver in the frames I checked. If you want the opening to read more clearly, I can widen the door or add a light spill.

I can also add a small bounce when the door opens, or a soft pulse on the glow once the lockup settles.
I added overshoot to the wordmark and the mark's slide, and pinned the door's pivot to its left edge. The critic now scores 90/100. It still flags the door pivot and the "moves once" note, which I left as they are.

items.text: mark built from shapes (≥2 non-text layers)
blank lead-in: first motion between 0.1 and 0.5 s
wordmark arrives after the mark, within the build (first visible 0.8-3.2 s)
final lockup held still ≥ 1.2 s (≥ 3 identical end frames)
one idea that comes from the mark itself (you can name its verb: opens, assembles, writes, becomes); not a generic pop/fade
wordmark enters from the mark (slides out from behind it under a mask, grows from a glyph, or is built from the same parts) and the mark makes room
snap and settle: hard decelerations (expo / spring), a small final move, one easing family
the door moves on its hinge (pivot at an edge, scale/rotation)
